raw_text:
Great. Here is a focused 3-week peaking block designed to taper volume, maintain or subtly hold intensity, and arrive fresh on meet day for your 28-year-old female intermediate recreational lifter with a powerlifting meet in 21 days. Assumptions: meet attempts will be in squat, bench, deadlift. Athlete is healthy, has a solid strength base, and is comfortable with these lifts. The plan emphasizes auto-regulation, technique crispness, and recovery while maintaining neural readiness.

Structure overview
- Week 1 (Day 1–7): Volume reduction with light to moderate sets, speed/technique emphasis, maintain intensity near meet targets but with lighter loads. Introduce optional deload feel and increased conditioning tolerance.
- Week 2 (Day 8–14): Further volume reduction, intensities near or at plan for meet attempts, focus on bar speed and RPE management, refine setup and commands, incorporate minimal specificity volume for confidence.
- Week 3 (Meet week): Taper to competition day. Very low volume, high quality reps, maximal freshness, ample recovery, nutrition strategy and meet-day ramp plan.

Weekly layout notes
- Training days: 4 days/week typical (e.g., Mon, Tue, Thu, Sat) to balance heavy lifting with recovery. If your client usually trains 5 days, you can keep 4 days and add light technique work or mobility on off days.
- Session goals: primary lifts (squat, bench, deadlift) with 1–2 accessory movements per lift, mostly light and technique-focused.
- Auto-regulation: adjust set/rep schemes by RPE as needed. If a given set feels strong, you can push for an extra rep or an additional set (within plan limits). If fatigued, cut back on volume even more.

Key parameters
- Meet day target loads: use planned competition attempts but back off in the weeks prior to ensure freshness. Consider targeting around 90–95% of estimated competition max for last warm-up sets, but avoid grinding.
- Density: keep warm-ups crisp; emphasize technique, speed on lower RPE sets, and bracing.

3-Week peaking block

Week 1: Volume reduction with technique + speed emphasis
Goal: Decrease overall training stress while preserving technique and neural drive.

Session A: Squat emphasis (Mon)
- Warm-up: 10 minutes easy cardio, dynamic hip/ankle mobility, squat-specific warm-ups
- Squat: 4 sets x 3 reps at RPE 7 (roughly 85–90% of 1RM aftermath planning), but capped at technical, not maximal. Focus on bar speed and depth.
- Back-off squat technique: 2 sets x 5 reps at RPE 7–7.5 with lighter load (e.g., 75–80% of top set practice)
- Front squat technical: 2 sets x 3 reps bodyweight-to-light load to reinforce upright torso and bar path (optional)
- Accessory (leg drive and mobility): Bulgarian split squats 2 x 6 each leg, glute bridges 3 x 8, hip flexor stretch

Session B: Bench emphasis (Tue)
- Warm-up: shoulder prep, scapular activation, light banded pec/clavicular work
- Bench press: 4 sets x 3 reps at RPE 7–7.5 (about 85–90%)
- Close-grip or incline bench: 2 x 5 reps at RPE 7
- Accessories: DB incline flyes 2 x 8, triceps pushdowns 3 x 8–10, overhead DB press 2 x 6
- Pause bench practice: 1 set x 2 reps paused at chest for rhythm (optional) 

Session C: Deadlift emphasis (Thu)
- Warm-up: hip hinge pattern work, mobility
- Deadlift: 4 sets x 3 reps at RPE 7–7.5 (around 85–90%)
- Deficit or tempo deadlifts: 2 x 3 reps at RPE 7 (optional, light)
- Barbell row or chest-supported row: 3 x 8
- Accessories: hamstring curls 3 x 8–10, back raises 3 x 12

Session D: Optional light technique/conditioning (Sat)
- Light technique work for all lifts: 2–3 sets of 2–3 reps at 60–70% 1RM focusing on speed and form
- Conditioning: 15–20 minutes of low-to-moderate intensity cardio or sled pushes

Notes for Week 1
- Keep total weekly volume down by 20–30% from peak week in accumulation phase; maintain movement quality.
- Emphasize bracing, foot position, and bar path.
- Sleep target: 7–9 hours per night; nutrition support: maintain protein 1.6–2.2 g/kg/day, ensure caloric intake supports recovery without excess fat gain.

Week 2: Intensity holds near meet targets with slight volume drop
Goal: Maintain intensity near competition values; reduce sets, keep reps 2–4 per work set with excellent form; sharpen tempo.

Session A: Squat emphasis (Mon)
- Warm-up
- Squat: 3 sets x 2–3 reps at RPE 8 (88–92%)
- Back-off: 2 x 3 reps at 70–75% (focus on speed)
- Accessory: Glute bridge 3 x 8, leg extensions 2 x 10, core work 2 x 12–15

Session B: Bench emphasis (Tue)
- Warm-up
- Bench: 3 sets x 2–3 reps at RPE 8 (88–92%)
- Pause bench or speed bench: 2 x 2 reps at 80–85% to maintain bench speed
- Accessories: DB row 3 x 8, triceps accessory 2 x 8, lateral raises 2 x 12

Session C: Deadlift emphasis (Thu)
- Warm-up
- Deadlift: 3 sets x 2–3 reps at RPE 8 (88–92%)
- Speed pulls or light deficit pulls: 2 x 2 reps at 65–70%
- Accessories: lat pulldown 3 x 8, glute-ham raise (or single-leg RDL) 3 x 6–8

Session D: Meet-specific plan or technique (Sat)
- Light technique focus: 2 sets x 2 reps of each main lift around 60–70% with emphasis on form and bar speed
- Optional short conditioning: 10–12 minutes easy cardio or sled work

Notes for Week 2
- Aim to maintain 85–95% intensity windows with 2–3 reps per set; keep volume lower than Week 1.
- Prioritize technical work under load; ensure crisp bracing and depth.
- Recovery: add deload-like measures (more mobility, contrast showers, increased sleep). Hydration.

Week 3: Meet week – taper and freshness for peak performance
Goal: Very low volume, high quality, maximal freshness. Physiological taper with mental readiness.

Session A: Squat refinement (Mon)
- Warm-up: brisk 5–8 minutes, mobility
- Squat: 2 sets x 2 reps at RPE 8 (target 90–95% of planned meet warm-up range)
- Optional: 1 set x 1 rep at 90–92% if feeling strong
- Accessory: light leg work only if necessary (e.g., 1 x 5 leg extension)

Session B: Bench refinement (Wed)
- Warm-up
- Bench: 2 sets x 2 reps at RPE 8 (target 90–95%)
- Optional: 1 x 1 rep at 90–92% if feeling strong
- Accessories: minimal; 1 x 6 row and 1 x 6 face pulls if needed for upper back health

Session C: Deadlift refinement (Fri)
- Warm-up
- Deadlift: 2 sets x 2 reps at RPE 8 (90–95%)
- Optional: 1 x 1 rep at 90% if confident
- Accessories: light hamstring and glute activation, 1 x 6 hyperextensions

Meet day plan (Day of competition)
- Pre-meet: 4–6 sets of light warm-ups across all main lifts at low RPE to prime CNS early
- Attempts: Follow coach’s call sheet; start with a conservative opener and progress as planned
- Bracing and technique: prioritize depth and bar path; use a consistent stance width and hip drive
- Recovery: post-meet nutrition: protein 1.6–2.2 g/kg/day, hydration, and a light cooldown/yoga session if possible

Nutrition and recovery notes for the 3-week peak
- Protein: maintain 1.6–2.2 g/kg/day to support recovery and muscle preservation.
- Carbohydrates: moderate to high on squat/bench/deadlift days prior to main lifts; taper to meet day with steady intake.
- Hydration: maintain euhydration; add electrolytes on heavy days.
- Sleep: target 7–9 hours nightly; consider short naps if needed.
- Recovery modalities: light mobility, contrast baths or contrast showers, massage or self-myofascial release as tolerated.

Progression and auto-regulation strategies
- If a lift feels strong on Week 3, you can add a single rep at 90–95% as a top set, but do not push beyond plan.
- If any pain or technique breakdown arises, reduce volume further and adjust intensity to keep form intact.
- If fatigue is excessive at any point, reduce the number of working sets for that lift and focus on technique.

Training summary
- Week 1: 4 sessions with 1–2 accessory movements per lift; volume down 20–30% from peak weeks; RPE targets 7–7.5 on main sets
- Week 2: 4 sessions with 2–3 reps per main lift at RPE 8; minimal volume; focus on speed and technique
- Week 3: 3–4 light sessions totaling minimal volume; main lifts at 2x2 or 1x1 at high but controlled intensity; meet-day strategy

I can also add a more detailed meet-day warm-up script and a specific nutrition plan aligned to her preferences.
